beats.text: Every single time Cursor or Claude writes code for you, your GPU wastes up to 70% of its compute doing nothing.
beats.visual_focus: A robot arm in a pristine lab vs. the same arm failing in a cluttered, real-world kitchen.

beats.text: Why? Because LLMs generate code one single token at a time—like a world-class chef who stops to ask you for salt before chopping every onion.
beats.visual_focus: A tangled web of neural connections labeled 'Overfitted Weights' snapping under pressure.

beats.text: Skill2Real solves this with a Proposer-Verifier-Governor loop. It uses ground-truth physics data from the simulator to validate motor skills, then freezes those low-level weights permanently.
beats.visual_focus: A three-node graph showing the PVG loop locking down a set of motor primitives.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: Finally, a video that doesn't treat me like I'm five. The hook in Beat 1 is solid—it hits the 'why' immediately without the 'today we are going to learn' fluff. I actually understood the architecture; treating the motor weights as a black-box library is a great way to describe freezing the weights. It feels like real engineering, not marketing garbage.
